reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the existence of isolated Pt/Pd sites, charge transfer to Pt/Pd, and their role in enhancing nitrobenzene hydrogenation. However, it provides no evidence that precursor mobility during synthesis controls site isolation, nor that modifying solvent viscosity or temperature achieves this. These mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles contain isolated Pt and Pd sites
Charge transfer occurs from base metals to Pt/Pd in the HEA
Isolated Pt/Pd sites and charge transfer enhance nitrobenzene adsorption and hydrogenation
Precursor mobility during solvothermal synthesis controls the degree of Pt/Pd site isolation
Increased solvent viscosity or lower temperature inhibits precursor mobility
